title: LA SB110: Prohibits using a child's image to train artificial intelligence to produce child sexual abuse materials. (8/1/26)

prohibitions: Using an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3)).

What it does

This law makes it a violation to use an image of a child under seventeen years old at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials. It also states that the child depicted does not have to be a natural person for an offense to occur. It provides factors for the trier of fact to determine age or apparent age in prosecutions.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who uses an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3)).

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • not stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • Using an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3)).

Penalties and enforcement

Enforcement is through prosecutions; the trier of fact may determine whether a natural person displayed or depicted was under seventeen or whether the image used to train an artificial intelligence model depicts a person who appears to be under seventeen, using listed factors (R.S. 14:81.1(G)). Penalties and any private right of action are not stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying artificial intelligence must not use images of children under seventeen years old at the time the image was created to train a model with the intent to produce child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3)).
  • The offense does not require the child depicted in the child sexual abuse materials to be a natural person, so synthetic or generated child images may still trigger liability if used as prohibited (R.S. 14:81.1(A)(4)).
  • In a prosecution, the trier of fact may determine whether the image used to train an artificial intelligence model depicts a person who appears to be under seventeen using factors such as body growth, bone structure, pubic or body hair, sexual organ development, context, expert testimony, and other probative information (R.S. 14:81.1(G)).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • Review training data pipelines to ensure no images of persons under seventeen years old are used for models that could produce child sexual abuse materials.
  • Implement age verification or content moderation for images in training datasets, especially for generative models.
  • Document the intended use of each artificial intelligence model to show absence of intent to produce child sexual abuse materials.
  • Train employees on the prohibition and on recognizing prohibited uses of child images in artificial intelligence training.
